related_questions.question: What is the early warning of a kidney stone?
related_questions.snippet: The most common symptom of kidney stones is pain in your lower back, belly or side (flank pain). It might feel like it extends from your groin to your side. It can be a dull pain or sharp and severe. It's sometimes called colicky pain because it can get worse in waves.

related_questions.question: What side of your body hurts with kidney stones?

text_blocks.snippet: Kidney stone pain is typically felt on either the right or left side of your back or flank, below the ribs and between the spine and the abdomen. The pain can also radiate to the lower abdomen, groin, or even the testicles in men or labia in women.
snippet_highlighted_words: either the right or left side of your back or flank, below the ribs and between the spine and the abdomen

list.title: Flank Pain:
list.snippet: Kidney stones often cause pain in the flank area, which is the side of your body between the ribs and the hip.

list.title: Back Pain:
list.snippet: You might also experience pain in your lower back, again, usually on one side, below the ribs and alongside your spine.

list.title: Pain Radiating:
list.snippet: The pain can travel from the flank or back down towards the lower abdomen and groin.

list.title: Other Locations:
list.snippet: Some people may experience pain near the bladder or even in the testicles (in men) or labia (in women) as the stone moves down the urinary tract.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that kidney stone pain can be intermittent, meaning it comes and goes, and can range from a dull ache to severe, sharp pain. If you're experiencing severe pain accompanied by fever, chills, or blood in your urine, seek immediate medical attention.
